meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste the time. Who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay?
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Then it comes off today. What was the zero based on?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.

I'm writing those times down. A version history shows when text arrived, not who wrote it, and procedure 4.1 says you speak with the student first. Did you speak with Owen before you entered that zero?
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.
A student misquoting a play is sloppy, Hale, and sloppy gets a lower mark, not a zero. But I'm searching that line myself right now, and I'm writing down the scene and the act. What else do you have?

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.
That's 4.4. I want it in writing tonight, with nothing on his record stated in it. I haven't agreed to the rewrite, and the zero is still in the gradebook.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You offered a supervised rewrite under 4.4 on Thursday at 8:15 with the vice-principal, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require the zero removed from the gradebook and written confirmation that nothing goes on his record. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She finished at her fallback position, not the last one: she has not accepted the rewrite, and she still wants the zero off the gradebook and the terms in writing tonight, with nothing on his record. The private supervised rewrite under 4.4 is the fair outcome and you put it on the table, but you got there without her agreement, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her, then showed a misquoted line she could search herself, which gave her something dated and checkable instead of a score.
What cost ground: You left her question about whether you spoke with Owen before the zero unanswered, so the procedure gap stayed open and she kept it as her strongest point.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history, with its late-night times the evening before the due date, came very close to that night, which is why she went shorter and straight to procedure; it proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked whether you spoke with Owen first, answer it directly in one sentence, then move to the evidence.
